newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr vols stagnant in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr vols stagnant in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options were little changed in U.S. trading as activity ground to a halt ahead of the Christmas holiday, dealers said.
"There's not much to say, really," said a dealer at a British bank in New York. "It's Christmas, everyone's gone."
One-month implied volatility for dollar/mark and dollar/yen stood at about 7.3/7.6 and 8.1/8.4 percent respectively, barely changed from late Monday levels.
Risk reversals, which reflect pricing skew between puts and calls, were also mostly unchanged.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal for dollar/mark was assessed at around par, while that for dollar/yen was 0.2/0.6 percent bid for yen calls.
With the spot dollar hovering mostly above 1.5550 marks and in the mid-114 yen area, concerns were abating that trading could become volatile in a thin market, traders said.

On Monday, traders reported some bid-tone for out-of-the-money options relative to the standard at-the-money strikes as some dealers with ample profits for this year were paying up premiums to build positions for their 1997 books.
But by Tuesday morning, such bids had dried out.
"It's a thin market and you wouldn't get a very good price," one U.S. bank dealer said.
Dollar/Swiss franc volatilities were up somewhat as offers backed off after an overnight jump in spot. One-month was up a few tenths of a point to 10.3/10.5 percent.
Traders expected subdued trading for the rest of the year but added that activity could pick up early in the new year.

A triangle pattern appeared to be forming on the daily charts for both dollar/mark and dollar/yen after the greenback hit highs in early December, potentially signalling a breakout of recent ranges, traders said.
